# VISION.md

The shared charter for every agent working on this project. An identical
copy sits at the root of every repository; the copy in the site repository
(`blakeaaronroberts.github.io`) is canonical. Every repository's `CLAUDE.md`
points here. If a repo's local instructions disagree with this file, stop and
tell Blake.

**Do not edit this file.** Only the Steward (the project's architect chat)
writes it, and only with Blake's approval. If you think it is wrong or out of date, tell Blake.

Status: DRAFT for Blake's review. Last updated 2026-11-12.
Interim code name: Rising Edge (placeholder; the suite will get its own name).

## 1. Vision

ECE is taught with static pictures of dynamic things. This project is an
open, free suite of tools for teaching 200–400 level electrical and computer
engineering in which **a concept is defined once and rendered everywhere**.

Each concept (a full adder, an RC circuit, a state machine) is described once
as a precise, executable source: a circuit, its parameters, and the simulation
that governs its behaviour. From that one source the suite produces:

- a textbook-quality static figure (SVG, PDF, LaTeX),
- an animation and a step-through slide,
- an interactive exploration in the browser,
- practice problems and autograded checks,
- a lab that connects it to real hardware.

Because every form comes from the same source, they always agree. Because
motion is driven by real simulation, the visuals never lie.

Every capability is also a standalone web tool on the site: nothing to
install, one job each, shared model and style, clean exports, documented API.

Non-goals: not a learning management system, no AI features for students, not
a commercial product, not a replacement for the instructor.

## 2. Principles

Use these to judge every idea.

- Visual intuition: show the mechanism.
- Active learning: students predict, manipulate, check.
- Real hardware: theory always lands on something physical.
- Industry relevance: the tools and workflows working engineers use.
- One source, many outputs; never redraw the same concept twice.
- One tool, one job; every tool usable on its own.
- Small, consistent, documented modules Blake can learn to build himself.
- Finished beats sprawling. Polish one piece before starting the next.

## 3. Constraints

- **Employer-agnostic.** No institution names, brand names, brand-colour
  names, work emails or work paths in code, identifiers, file names or
  folder names. Institution branding exists only as a swappable theme.
- **Privacy.** No student data in any repository. Anything that touches
  grading or labs is designed so student records never enter a repo.
- **Free and open-source tools only**, for building and for using the suite.
  This includes fonts.
- **Windows-first** for local work; **browser-first** for public tools.
- **Static hosting.** The site is GitHub Pages. Tools run in the browser
  (JavaScript, WebAssembly) or serve prebuilt outputs. Anything that needs a
  server is a separate service, with the trade-off written down.
- **Licence: not yet chosen.** Do not add LICENSE files, licence headers or
  licence badges until Blake decides.
- **Approval.** Blake signs off on anything students or the public see.
  Agents mark something approved only when Blake directly tells them to
  (see section 7).

## 4. Architecture

Four layers. Everything above layer 2 depends on the core model, never on
another product.

1. **Sources.** CircuiTikZ symbols, KiCad schematics, HDL, SPICE netlists,
   parameters. What a concept is.
2. **Core model.** Circuits as graphs of elements and pins, signals over
   time, simulation results, and one style system with swappable themes.
3. **Renderers.** Static figures, animations, slides, web interactives,
   problem generators, lab checks.
4. **Web tools and products.** Toolbox, Studio (authoring workflow),
   Explorations (interactive essays), Practice, Labs.

### Core model (decided 2026-11-11)

The core model is renderer-independent. It must not import Manim.

- **Circuit schema (JSON).** Elements with type, position and rotation;
  named pins; nets (which pins connect); wire routes; parameters. A schema
  file can be validated, simulated and rendered without any drawing library.
- **Symbol pack.** The toolbox exports each approved element as an SVG plus
  its pin coordinates and grid metadata. Browser tools draw with the symbol
  pack, so web output matches the LaTeX and animation output exactly.
- **Two consumers.** Python (Manim animations, LaTeX export) and JavaScript
  (web tools). Both read the same schema and the same symbol pack.
- **Simulation** produces signals over time from the schema (logic
  evaluation first; SPICE and HDL simulation later). Renderers consume those
  signals; no renderer invents its own behaviour.

Today the toolbox's `Circuit` is a Manim object that stores geometry only.
Moving to the schema is Phase 0 work. Propose the schema to Blake before
building on it.

## 5. Repository map

| Repository | Role | Visibility |
|---|---|---|
| `blakeaaronroberts.github.io` | Quarto site: the suite's public home, explorations, web tools, docs, this file | Public |
| `manimations` | The animation library and working folder for all animated work: circuit toolbox (CircuiTikZ symbols + Manim wires and motion), gallery, exports | Private for now |

`manimations` is the name of the animation library, not of the suite. Where
the circuit schema, symbol pack and browser-side code live is an open
decision (section 9). Do not create new repositories without Blake's say-so.

## 6. Current phase and goals

**Phase 0, Foundation** (now): toolbox core, shared style with themes, the
circuit schema and symbol pack, this file, repo map.

**Phase 1, Proving ground** (year-one definition of success): one full
digital logic course done end to end (figures, animations, slides), plus a
public site with a polished set of explorations and the first web tools.

Immediate targets, in order:

1. **First flagship: the 4-bit ripple-carry adder**, shown on one public page
   as a static figure, an animation of the carry rippling against a timing
   diagram, and a browser interactive where the reader flips input bits and
   watches the carry propagate. All three come from one schema file. Scope
   fence: ripple-carry only; carry-lookahead is a follow-up.
2. **Site launch.** The public build stays a landing page until the flagship
   exploration and a project page explaining the suite both exist.
3. **The course run.** Figures, animations and slides for the full digital
   logic course, built with the same pipeline.

Later phases: 2 Interaction (more web tools, KiCad import, practice and
autograding). 3 Hardware and breadth (remote FPGA lab, other course areas,
lecture video pipeline). 4 Adoption. Do not start later-phase work early.

## 7. Shared conventions

### Style system
- One settings file per repo is the only place colours, line weights, sizes,
  grid and fonts are defined. Everything else reads from it or is generated
  from it. No hard-coded colours or sizes anywhere.
- Colours are referenced by role (ink, low, high, flow, accent, background),
  never by hue or by brand. Only the style file maps roles to colours.
- **Default theme:** the Okabe-Ito palette (`high` is vermillion, #D55E00)
  everywhere. Colour roles are shared by every medium; fonts are set per
  medium (next bullet). Defaults, exports, galleries and committed renders
  always use this theme.
- **Maths is STIX Two everywhere (Blake, 2026-11-12: this is a priority).**
  A formula must look the same in a figure, an animation, a slide, a site
  page and a web tool. Text fonts may differ by medium; maths may not.

  | Medium | Maths | Text | Names on elements |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | LaTeX outputs: figures, exports, animations, slides | STIX Two Math | STIX Two Text | Fira Mono |
  | Site pages | MathJax 4 with its `mathjax-stix2` font | The site theme's fonts | n/a |
  | Web tools | MathJax 4 with its `mathjax-stix2` font | The site theme's fonts | Symbol-pack SVGs |

  - The LaTeX fonts ship with MiKTeX and TeX Live, so a Linux CI runner
    renders identically.
  - On the web, load MathJax 4's single-file bundle that includes the STIX2
    font (`tex-mml-chtml-mathjax-stix2.js` from the `@mathjax/mathjax-stix2-font`
    package) through Quarto's `html-math-method` `url`. Pin the version;
    never use a floating `@4` URL. Web tools load the same file.
  - Quarto's own default is MathJax 3, which has no STIX Two font. Switching
    to MathJax 4 must keep equation numbering, IEEE-style equation
    references and dark mode working; if any of them breaks, stop and tell
    Blake rather than working around it.
  - Figures placed on the site or in a web tool are SVGs whose glyphs are
    outlines, so they keep the LaTeX fonts in every browser.
  - The suite stays on LaTeX (CircuiTikZ) for figures. Do not introduce a
    second typesetting system to solve font matching.
- **Private themes** (such as an institution's look for Blake's own slides)
  live in a git-ignored folder and are selected at render time. Never commit
  one, and never name a proprietary font or brand colour in committed code.
- All on-screen words go through LaTeX, so fonts come from the style file
  with nothing installed by hand.
- Palettes must be colour-blind safe. Signal state must not rely on colour
  alone in web tools (add a label, pattern or value readout).

### Language
- Use kind, inclusive, respectful language everywhere: code, identifiers,
  comments, docs, commit messages, UI text, figures and course material.
- Prefer current, descriptive terms over outdated ones: leader/follower (not
  master/slave) for latches, flip-flops and buses; primary/secondary or
  controller/peripheral for devices; allowlist/denylist; `main` as the
  default branch; placeholder or stub (not dummy); check or smoke test.
- When a datasheet, standard or textbook uses an older term, use the current
  term and mention the older one once where students need to recognise it
  (e.g. "controller (older texts: master)").
- Student-facing text is encouraging and never belittling: no "simply",
  "obviously" or "trivially".

### Approval gates
- Every element, figure, tool and page starts as a draft.
- Only Blake decides what is approved. An agent writes "approved" in a
  registry or front matter only when Blake directly tells it to in the
  conversation, for the specific items he names. Never on the agent's own
  judgement, and never as a side effect of other work.
- Circuits and public pages use approved elements only. If something new is
  needed, add it as a draft and stop for review.
- Look at your own render before handing work over.

### Documentation
- Every repo has a `README.md` (what it is, how to run it) and a `CLAUDE.md`
  that points to this file and adds only repo-specific rules.
- Every extension point has a short HOW_TO guide written so Blake can do it
  by hand. Update the guide in the same change that alters the pattern.
- Record notable choices in a `DECISIONS.md` in the repo where they apply:
  date, decision, reason.

### Testing and CI
- Tests cover the core model first: schema validation, connectivity,
  simulation results.
- Render checks run in CI: every approved element and example circuit must
  compile, and its output is compared against a stored reference.
- CI must run on a free Linux runner, which is one reason the default theme
  uses open fonts.

### Web-tool structure (proposed; confirm with Blake before the first tool)
- One folder per tool on the site, usable on its own page and embeddable in
  an exploration.
- Reads the circuit schema, the symbol pack and the shared theme tokens.
  No tool carries its own copy of a symbol or a colour.
- Exports SVG at minimum. Keyboard-usable. Alt text and captions on every
  figure.
- A short README per tool documenting its inputs, outputs and API.

## 8. How work flows

- Blake talks to each agent directly. A separate chat, the **Steward**, reads
  the repositories and reports to Blake. It does not instruct agents. The one file
  it writes is `VISION.md`, kept identical in every repository, and only with
  Blake's approval. It touches nothing else in any repository.
- Plan first for architectural steps; build in batches with a review stop
  between batches.
- Blake has a few hours a week. Prefer the smallest change that moves a
  current-phase goal, and stop for review rather than building ahead.

## 9. Open decisions (do not assume an answer)

- Software licence.
- The suite's real name.
- Where the circuit schema, symbol pack and browser code live: inside
  `manimations`, in the site repo, or in a new repository.
- Whether the site's current third-party timing-diagram and circuit
  embeds stay as an interim or are replaced by suite tools.

Settled: circuits always come from the toolbox; LaTeX figures are only for
non-circuit figures such as timing diagrams and plots (2026-11-12).
